item.title: Comprehensive Survey: Remote Desktop and Remote Terminal Technologies
item.description: Operating one machine from another decomposes into three engineering problems: getting the remote screen to your display (rendering), sending your keyboard and mouse over (input), and establishing a channel between the two machines that survives NAT (connectivity). The first two produced RDP, VNC, and SSH; the third produced ID-based addressing, hole punching, and relay networks. This article maps the remote desktop and remote terminal landscape along these lines: the split between two rendering routes, the evolution of RDP’s graphics pipeline, the Wayland shake-up on Linux desktops, the connection logic of commercial products and RustDesk, the SSH ecosystem’s answers to disconnection, enterprise access layers, and the KVM-over-IP layer below the operating system.

item.title: A Detailed Comparison of Remote Access Products and Open-Source Projects
item.description: A Comprehensive Survey of Remote Desktop and Remote Terminal Technologies covers the technical landscape and the security-incident reviews, and RDP Protocol Deep Dive goes down to one protocol’s wire format. This post does one thing: put well-known products and open-source projects against the same set of dimensions — connection architecture, codecs, encryption, self-hostability, license, activity. Table first, commentary after. Data time point is October 2026; GitHub stars and licenses were fetched via the GitHub API, product behavior comes from official documentation and security advisories, and no benchmark measurements are included.

item.title: MiBeeReach: Remote Desktop, Terminal, SSH and Tunneling in One Binary
item.description: My complaints about commercial remote-access software are specific: the free tier throttles speed and caps hours, ads pop up on schedule, traffic flows through the vendor’s servers, and not one knob for image quality or latency belongs to me. I used Sunflower and ToDesk for a while and evaluated self-hosting RustDesk’s server edition before deciding to build one from zero. That is MiBeeReach: a single-binary remote access platform in Rust with remote desktop, remote terminal, remote SSH, tunneling, and cross-network P2P all inside. The name joins the MiBee brand with Reach — making any machine behind NAT reachable from outside, on your terms.
